newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures still down late with soft cash.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures still down late with soft cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained lower late Tuesday in moderate trade, still pressured by softer September cash prices though some said the market was oversold and due for a technical bounce.
At 1430 EDT, October was down by 3.2 cents at $1.905 per million British thermal units, while November was still 2.9 cents lower at $2.06. Others were off by one to three cents.

"Cash came off and the hurricane (Edouard) isn't doing anything, but technically, the market is oversold and should rebound," said one Houston-based cash trader, adding weather forecasts were not very supportive.

At 1100 EDT, Hurricane Edouard, was 305 miles northeast of the Leeward Islands, moving west-northwest at 15 mph with winds of 130 mph. Forecasters expected the storm to move north of the Caribbean islands but were not sure if it posed a threat to the U.S. mainland.

While traders agreed the market could stage a short-term technical bounce, they said Monday's breakdown will likely lead to more selling without better fundamental support. They pegged October support in the $1.88 area, with resistance seen near $2.10.
U.S. Gulf Coast September prices slipped five cents or more Tuesday to the $1.75-1.80 area. Sept Midcon pipes were off almost a dime to the mid-to-high $1.60s.
Most pipeline nomination deadlines expire today and Wednesday.

NYMEX said 20,626 Henry Hub contracts traded at 1410 EDT. NYMEX September Permian natgas tumbled 6.5 cents to another contract low of $1.575, while deferreds were still untraded at 1440 EDT. NYMEX said eight Permian contracts traded at 1410 EDT.
NYMEX September Permian natgas futures expire Wednesday August 28.
On the KCBT, September was still six cents lower at $1.625, while most deferreds were steady to down 4.5 cents. The October East/West spread widened by 1.3 cents to 20.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
KCBT September natgas futures expire today.
